title: Treewidth-connectivity partition conjecture for graphs
statement: Let $G$ be a graph, and let $k$ be an integer such that $G$ has treewidth at most $k$ and connectivity at least $k$. A vertex set inducing a graph of treewidth at most $k-1$ and connectivity at least $k-1$ is denoted by $\mathcal{T}$, and an independent set is denoted by $\mathcal{I}$. **Treewidth-connectivity partition conjecture.** The vertices of $G$ can be partitioned into an induced graph $\mathcal{T}$ of treewidth at most $k-1$ and connectivity at least $k-1$, and an independent set $\mathcal{I}$. This is proposed as a generalization of a theorem for graphs of treewidth at most $2$; the source leaves it as a belief rather than an established result.
source_name: Stijn Cambie, François Dross, Kolja Knauer, Hoang La and Petru Valicov, “Partitions of planar (oriented) graphs into a connected acyclic and an independent set”, arXiv:2412.11774 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.11774

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of December 2024). “On the other hand, planarity is also essential, as shown by Horton who disproved a corresponding conjecture of Tutte .”
